correctness.rationale: JR fails exactly if some outside candidate has q_n or more supporters among the uncovered voters. Given the columns of a fixed quota-exact committee, the uncovered set has at most n−q_n voters, and an outside candidate's uncovered count is binomial with that many or fewer trials. For p_n≤1/k+1/(4k²), the gap from its mean to q_n is at least n/(2k²), so Hoeffding gives exp(−n/(2k⁴)) per pair, with probability zero if there are no uncovered voters. Union-bounding gives the claimed simultaneous relation, also when m_n=k. The quota-column count is exactly binomial by independence. For x=q_n/n, Stirling gives (2πnx(1−x))^(−1/2) exp(−n D(x||p_n))(1+o(1)), with nD(x||p_n)→λ²/(2v_k) and x(1−x)→v_k; rounding contributes only O(1/n) to x. This proves the stated local constant. The quota count converges to Poisson at finite supply ratio, including zero; the simultaneous relation transfers both counts and the existence event. Bounding the count discrepancy by C(m_n,k) on the bad event and using the binomial factorial moment proves the claimed mean convergence. At diverging supply the binomial mean diverges and its variance is at most its mean. At fixed p≠1/k, positive relative entropy defeats polynomial supply. The supplied script checks only finite instances and numerical diagnostics; it was inspected, not run, and the proof does not rely on it.

evidence: Elkind et al. use per-voter probability p(1−p)^s of approving an outsider but no member of a group of size s. Proposition 1 bounds the maximum of this probability by 1/(2s) for s>0, and concludes every size-k committee is JR with high probability for the stated fixed-parameter regime.

The Resultary theorem states the square-root supply regimes and matching count/existence limits with an additional o(n^(−1/2)) term allowed in approval propensity, and gives an exponential finite coupling bound.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Elkind et al.'s fixed-parameter theorem alone does not state a DR count. But the proof's uniform bound for s=k gives a binomial mean at most n/(2k) for each W,d in the moving window too. The event of q_n or more uncovered supporters has probability at most exp(−n/(2k²)) by Hoeffding. The same union factor C(m_n,k)(m_n−k) therefore gives a stronger unconditional bound for all committees, with no exact-quota conditioning required. Polynomial growth is absorbed by the fixed exponential gap.
